Given the diagram above, where $|a|=5\sqrt{3}$ and $|b|=6,$ find the **exact** value of $|a+b|.$

$|a+b|=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the triangle law for adding the vectors $a$ and $b.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251309/assets/c58fcaace0fd6b1161426357025da18aaccd182b7035db152221bdfddbe28226.png)

Using the law of cosines, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+b{|}^{2} & =|a{|}^{2}+|b{|}^{2}-2|a||b|\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =(5\sqrt{3})^{2}+{6}^{2}-2\cdot (5\sqrt{3})\cdot 6\cdot \,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =75+36+90 \\  & =201.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get

$$
|a+b|=\sqrt{201}.
$$
